0.long_answer: The disease most commonly associated with Fanconi syndrome in children is cystinosis. Cystinosis is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by the accumulation of cystine in lysosomes due to defective cystine transport. This condition is caused by mutations in the CTNS gene, which encodes the lysosomal membrane protein cystinosin. The defect in cystinosin leads to intracellular cystine accumulation, causing damage to various tissues, including the kidneys, where it results in the proximal tubular dysfunction observed in Fanconi syndrome.
